name: 217 East Twentieth Street — red brick corner rowhouse with a copper oriel, K01 frontage assembly

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3½ brick dwelling (D) with a rounded bay at its street corner, a frame strip across the middle of its plan and a 3-storey rear range with a cut corner'. Carried to 1904 on the T-2982 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: T-3781 (piece 1 of T-1939, the X01 package of the T-1837 programme) refines the district draft (T-2982) in place under the same id: the house is rebuilt from the K01 frontage assembly and its kits — a K03 red pressed-brick body over a sandstone base course, a round K08 oriel sheathed in copper corbelled out at the street front's east corner over the ground storey, K06 sash, a K07 door, a steep slated hip and the 3-storey rear range — instead of the draft builder. What is read: sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (the outline, '3½', the front's bowed east end, the '3' rear range) and three 2009 photographs of the surviving house (forms only). What is not built, and why, is the liberty L-k01-217-e20th-3781; T-3783 solves the photographs' cameras and works the match down.

documented_range.note: The house claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-2982 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped); the 2009 photographs show it standing. No building or loss date is read for it here (T-3781).

position.symbolic_location: 217 E. Twentieth Street, parcel e20th_217 (data/street_grid/1904.json), south side of East Twentieth Street, the district's named context buildings off Prairie Avenue: East Twentieth Street between Indiana and Prairie, and Calumet Avenue between 20th and 21st Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body at its east wall: row 350 and column 437.5 of sheet 35 at full size (T-3781), 7.9 m behind and 0.31 m east of the draft's corner (the draft's fit had read a 6.75 m deep front block and set the rest as a range), carried through the T-1250 fit of the sheet (0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom, plus about a pixel, 0.19 m, of reading). Rotation -90.599 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line, north to East Twentieth Street, as the draft had it; v runs west from the east wall, so K01's `south` wall is the house's east flank on the 20 ft passage and its `north` wall the west one, toward 215.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: 14.6 m from the rear wall (row 350, where the outline narrows to the rear range) to the front (row 271.5, on the street line), and 7.06 m along the front from the east wall (column 437.5, on the 20 ft passage) to the west wall (column 399.5, the lot line with 215), read off sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn at full size (T-3781) at 0.1858 m a pixel. The sheet draws a yellow (frame) strip across the plan about 6.4 m behind the front: not built, the body is one brick block (L-k01-217-e20th-3781). The front's east end bows out about 0.8 m over the street line (rows 267-271, columns 419-437): the corner oriel (see bays).

stories.note: '3½' printed on the 1911 sheet over the front: three full storeys and a half storey in the roof.

construction.note: The 1911 sheet colours the house pink (brick); the 2009 photographs show red pressed brick over a base course of red sandstone, with stone sills, heads and the door's carved surround (the register's '213/217 red brick and sandstone').

principal_floor_m.note: The principal floor low over the walk: in photograph 223 the door's sill stands a step or two over the walk and the round-headed lights' sills about a metre over it; 0.55 m, three risers, its exact height unread (T-3783 solves the camera).

storey_heights_m.note: Three storeys of about 3.8, 3.4 and 3.2 m: in photograph 220 the ground storey's round heads, the oriel's two tiers of lights and the stone courses between them divide the east flank about 3.8 : 3.4 : 3.2; storey heights in the street's usual range. T-3783 holds them to the pictures.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A brick front on a stone base: the contract's masonry starting thickness; no source measures it.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A 13 in brick side wall, the contract's ordinary masonry thickness; no source measures it.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: A shallow top step before the door: the front stands on the street line and the stoop stays inside the strip before the walk (front_yard_m); its depth unread.

eave_overhang_m.note: The hip's eave 0.3 m out, its depth unread: no photograph shows the main roof's eave behind the gable.

service_wall_brick.note: The kit's common panel under the face brick: the walls are laid in the front's red pressed brick all round (face_brick).

face_brick.note: Red pressed brick in fine joints over the base course on the front and on the east flank in photographs 106, 220 and 223 (the register's red brick for 213 and 217): the palette's pressed red, laid all round; the west and rear walls, which no picture shows, are laid the same.

stone_front.note: Large smooth sandstone blocks under the ground storey's lights in photograph 223, brick over them from the principal floor: K02's brown sandstone stands in for the photographs' red, which the kit does not stock (L-k01-217-e20th-3781).

street_front_round_heads.note: The ground storey's two lights under the oriel are round-headed in photographs 220 and 223, their heads turned in brick; a small key at each crown is reconstructed (the 400 px prints do not resolve one).

street_front_trim.note: Plain stone heads and sills over the upper storeys' lights in photographs 106 and 220.

wall_head.note: No cornice on the front reads in any picture; the hip's eave stands on the wall head.

roof_form.note: A steep hip over the main body: '3½' on the sheet puts a half storey in the roof, and photograph 106 shows a steep slated roof over the east flank; the gable it rises to is not built (L-k01-217-e20th-3781).

roof_pitch_deg.note: A steep pitch for the half storey in the roof, the contract's steepest hip (45 degrees); the gable's rakes in photograph 106 stand steeper, unmeasured.

roof_covering.note: Slate on the roof over the east flank in photograph 106, its rakes and the oriel's cornice in copper.

stoop_width_m.note: A short stoop at the door, its width unread.

entrance_bay.note: The door is in the street front west of the oriel's two round-headed lights in photograph 223: K01's `north` end, toward 215.

front_bays.note: The street front, counted from the east corner: the two round-headed lights under the oriel (photograph 223) and the door's axis west of them; the upper storeys' lights over the door.

side_bays.note: The east flank's lights: photograph 220 shows one bay of lights in three storeys near the front, a large round-headed light on the ground storey; the rest of the flank is unseen and its bays reconstructed.

north_bays.note: No lights in the west wall: it stands on the lot line against 215.

rear_bays.note: One light in the rear wall west of the rear range: unseen.

sash_by_storey.note: The side and rear lights: the kit's ordinary sash, storey by storey.

basement_lights.note: A low basement grille in the base course under the round-headed lights in photograph 223.

window_kit.note: Two-over-two sash, the round-headed lights under a fanlight; the 2009 sash and grilles are not read as 1904's.

entrance_kit.note: The door in the street front behind its carved sandstone surround in photograph 223, a step or two over the walk, the front on the street line: the kit's panelled door on a short stoop in the 1.6 m strip between the front and the walk's inner edge (data/street_section/1904.json, the 6 ft walk's crossings on this face); the surround's carving is not built (L-k01-217-e20th-3781).

windows.why_not_ordinary: the oriel's lights bent round it in photographs 106 and 220, three a storey
the oriel's upper tier of lights in photographs 106 and 220

bays.note: The corner oriel: in photographs 106, 220 and 223 a round bay sheathed in copper stands out over the ground storey at the street front's east corner, on a rounded copper underside over the two round-headed lights, two storeys of lights bent round it under a copper cornice; the 1911 sheet bows the front's east end out about 0.8 m over 3.4 m (rows 267-271). Built as K08's round oriel in copper on the second floor, 3.2 m on its chord and 0.8 m out, its centre 1.9 m from the east corner: K01 keeps 0.3 m of wall between a bay and its corner, where the photographs' oriel turns the corner onto the east flank (L-k01-217-e20th-3781). Its cap is a low copper cone; the photographs' green is 2009's patina.

chimneys.note: One stack against the west wall: no picture shows the stacks.

rainwater.note: The kit's half-round copper gutter on the hip's eaves, a pipe down the east flank's rear end.

boundary.note: A low iron railing on a stone curb along the walk's inner edge, 1.55 m before the front, with a walk gate: the strip before the front is enclosed in photographs 223 and 224 along this row (215's railing), but no picture shows 217's in 1904; the kit's spear railing, its pattern unread. The lot lines are the sheet's (columns 399.2 and 437.6).

yard.note: A short walk of stone flags across the strip from the public walk to the stoop's foot, as the street's other K01 fronts; the strip's 2009 planting is not read as 1904's.

rear_wings.note: The sheet's '3' rear range behind the main body on its east side: rows 350-377, columns 409-437.5 (5.0 m deep, 5.3 m wide), its south-west corner cut on the diagonal (built square, L-k01-217-e20th-3781). Flat-roofed, its storeys the main body's.
